summary.intent: Make a first-release package whose name is already taken on the registry (e.g. crates.io) by someone else produce a clear, dedicated error instead of reading as 'already published'. This was the next item after opening PR #353.
summary.outcome: Implemented a taken-name check for first releases with a new error code (E322), a shared repository comparison helper, unit tests, spec/docs/changeset updates, and a passing full CI. Verified against a real crates.io collision and opened a new PR; PR #353, which still has a merge conflict, was left to resolve next.

repo: Error codes are defined in crates/callisto-graph/src/error.rs and documented in docs/errors.md, where rows must stay in numeric order and a count line must be bumped when adding a code.
Release behavior is specified in docs/specs/release.json with criteria IDs like REL-PUB-14; new behavior extends or adds criteria there.
Changes need a changeset file in .claude/changeset/ style dir (.changeset/*.md) before shipping.

The foreign-repository adoption warning and the new taken-name check share a repository comparison helper in provider/repository.rs; the registry module and repository module needed crate visibility changes to be reused.
plan_workspace_release and plan_local_release have multiple callers (including the init preview), so adding a check there affects init tests too.
A fake cargo harness is used in tests/e2e to simulate `cargo info` output and repository parsing.

code.finding: Registry observation errors must be treated as 'can't tell' rather than failing the plan; the taken-name check must not fail when a registry is unreachable.
Repository comparison logic was refactored into a shared helper so both the foreign-repo warning and the taken-name check use it.

workflow: Running the full CI pipeline after each change surfaced regressions in the init preview test and a local.rs test that targeted code paths affected by the new check.
Verifying against a real-world crates.io name collision gave end-to-end confidence beyond the fake-registry tests.
When several PRs are open, checking mergeability first helped decide to ship the finished branch before resolving the conflicted one.

friction: Inserted E322 before E321 in errors.md and had to reorder the rows.
The first CI run failed on the init test because the new check altered plan_workspace_release callers.
A second CI failure showed the check failed plans when the registry was unreachable, requiring a fix to treat observation errors as unknown.
Module visibility and import errors required several build-fix iterations.
open_items: PR #353 still has a merge conflict that needs resolving.
The new taken-name PR is open and awaiting review/merge.
